claims.title: Rome annexes Dardania
claims.summary: The kingdom of the Dardani in the central Balkans was absorbed by Rome and incorporated into the province of Moesia, with towns such as Ulpiana, Scupi and Naissus as regional centres.

sources.label: History of Kosovo (ancient Dardania to the medieval period)

claims.title: Province of Dardania
claims.summary: In the administrative reorganisation of the later Roman Empire, the region was constituted as a province again bearing the ancient name of Dardania, within the diocese of Moesia.

sources.label: History of Kosovo (ancient Dardania to the medieval period)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-284-province-of-dardania, claim TL:KOS:event:284:province-of-dardania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slavic settlement of the interior
claims.summary: As the Danube frontier collapsed, Slavic peoples settled widely across the Balkan interior under and after Byzantine authority, transforming the population of the future Kosovo.

sources.label: History of Kosovo (ancient Dardania to the medieval period)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-600-slavic-settlement-of-the-interior, claim TL:KOS:event:600:slavic-settlement-of-the-interior, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Byzantine and Bulgarian borderland
claims.summary: The region passed between the Byzantine Empire, the First Bulgarian Empire and rising Serbian principalities, a contested frontier of the medieval Balkans before the Nemanjic ascendancy.

sources.label: History of Kosovo (ancient Dardania to the medieval period)
Kosovo: History

claims.title: Nemanjic rule and the Serbian Church
claims.summary: The Nemanjic dynasty consolidated its hold over the region, which became a centre of the medieval Serbian state and of the autocephalous Serbian Orthodox Church seated at the Patriarchate of Pec.

sources.label: History of Kosovo (ancient Dardania to the medieval period)
Kosovo: History

claims.title: Gracanica and Visoki Decani built
claims.summary: The monastery of Gracanica was founded in 1321 and Visoki Decani built in the mid-14th century for King Stefan Decanski; with other churches they form the UNESCO Medieval Monuments in Kosovo, later placed on the List of World Heritage in Danger.

sources.label: Medieval Monuments in Kosovo (World Heritage List, no. 724)
Medieval Monuments in Kosovo: State of Conservation (List of World Heritage in Danger since 2006)

claims.title: The Battle of Kosovo
claims.summary: At Kosovo Polje, the Field of Blackbirds, the Serbian prince Lazar and his allies fought the Ottoman sultan Murad I; both rulers died and the Ottoman victory led to the eventual subjugation of Serbia.

sources.label: Battle of Kosovo (1389)
The Battle of Kosovo, 1389

claims.title: Ottoman conquest completed
claims.summary: By the mid-15th century the Ottomans had established direct rule over all of Serbia, including Kosovo, ending the medieval Serbian state in the region.

sources.label: Kosovo: History

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-1455-ottoman-conquest-completed, claim TL:KOS:event:1455:ottoman-conquest-completed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman administration of Kosovo
claims.summary: For roughly four and a half centuries Kosovo was ruled as part of the Ottoman Empire, governed through the Balkan provinces and, latterly, the vilayet of Kosovo.

sources.label: Kosovo: History

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-1455-ottoman-administration-of-kosovo, claim TL:KOS:event:1455:ottoman-administration-of-kosovo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Migrations and a shifting population
claims.summary: Over the Ottoman centuries many Orthodox Serbs emigrated and parts of the population converted to Islam, while the Albanian-speaking share grew, probably forming a majority by the 18th century.

sources.label: Kosovo: History

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-1690-migrations-and-a-shifting-population, claim TL:KOS:event:1690:migrations-and-a-shifting-population, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The League of Prizren
claims.summary: Albanian leaders founded the League of Prizren in Kosovo, the first Albanian nationalist organisation, seeking to unite Albanian-inhabited lands and promote the Albanian language amid the Congress of Berlin's partition plans.

sources.label: Albanian League (League of Prizren, 1878)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-1878-the-league-of-prizren, claim TL:KOS:event:1878:the-league-of-prizren, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Suppression of the League
claims.summary: After resisting territorial transfers to Montenegro and Greece, the League of Prizren was suppressed by the Ottoman authorities, but it had laid the foundation of the Albanian national movement.

sources.label: Albanian League (League of Prizren, 1878)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-1881-suppression-of-the-league, claim TL:KOS:event:1881:suppression-of-the-league, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Balkan Wars bring Kosovo into Serbia
claims.summary: The Balkan Wars ended Ottoman rule, and Kosovo was incorporated into the Kingdom of Serbia, later part of the Yugoslav state.

sources.label: Kosovo: History

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-1912-balkan-wars-bring-kosovo-into-serbia, claim TL:KOS:event:1912:balkan-wars-bring-kosovo-into-serbia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Wide autonomy under the Yugoslav constitution
claims.summary: The 1974 Yugoslav constitution gave Kosovo broad self-government as an autonomous province within Serbia, with its own assembly, courts and a veto, making it nearly a republic in practice.

sources.label: Kosovo: Government and society (autonomy and the 1974 constitution)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-1974-wide-autonomy-under-the-yugoslav-constitution, claim TL:KOS:event:1974:wide-autonomy-under-the-yugoslav-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pristina student protests
claims.summary: Student demonstrations in Pristina demanding republic status for Kosovo grew into wider unrest, which the Yugoslav authorities suppressed, exposing deep tensions over the province's status.

sources.label: Kosovo: Government and society (autonomy and the 1974 constitution)
Kosovo: History

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kosovo: From ancient Dardania to a contested independence at the crossroads of the Balkans.", terralore.co/country/KOS/chronicle#ev-1981-pristina-student-protests, claim TL:KOS:event:1981:pristina-student-protests, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Milosevic revokes Kosovo's autonomy
claims.summary: Under Slobodan Milosevic, the Serbian assembly stripped Kosovo of most of the autonomy granted in 1974, returning police, courts, education and language policy to Belgrade and igniting Albanian resistance.

sources.label: Kosovo: Government and society (autonomy and the 1974 constitution)
Kosovo: History
Kosovo (US recognition, 18 February 2008; diplomatic history)

claims.title: The Albanian parallel state
claims.summary: Led by Ibrahim Rugova and the Democratic League of Kosovo, Kosovo's Albanians boycotted Serbian institutions and ran their own parallel schools, clinics and administration in a decade of nonviolent resistance.

sources.label: Ibrahim Rugova, Sakharov Prize 1998

claims.title: KLA insurgency and Serbian crackdown
claims.summary: The Kosovo Liberation Army's insurgency against Serbian rule met an escalating campaign by Serbian and Yugoslav forces, killing many Albanians and displacing hundreds of thousands during 1998.

sources.label: Kosovo conflict (1998-99 war and NATO intervention)
NATO's role in Kosovo (KFOR; Operation Allied Force, 1999)
Under Orders: War Crimes in Kosovo (1998-99 expulsions and killings)

claims.title: NATO air campaign begins
claims.summary: After the failure of talks at Rambouillet, NATO launched Operation Allied Force against Yugoslav forces on 24 March 1999, a 78-day air campaign intended to halt the humanitarian catastrophe in Kosovo.

sources.label: NATO's role in Kosovo (KFOR; Operation Allied Force, 1999)

claims.title: Mass expulsion of Kosovo Albanians
claims.summary: Serbian and Yugoslav forces forcibly expelled some 862,000 ethnic Albanians from Kosovo, uprooting more than 80 percent of the population, with thousands killed in a systematic campaign later prosecuted as war crimes.

sources.label: Under Orders: War Crimes in Kosovo (1998-99 expulsions and killings)

claims.title: UN Resolution 1244 and UNMIK
claims.summary: The Security Council adopted Resolution 1244, ending the war, placing Kosovo under UN interim administration (UNMIK) with a NATO-led KFOR security force, while reaffirming Yugoslav sovereignty and deferring final status.

sources.label: United Nations Security Council Resolution 1244 (10 June 1999)
NATO's role in Kosovo (KFOR; Operation Allied Force, 1999)

claims.title: Constitutional Framework for self-government
claims.summary: UNMIK established a Constitutional Framework for Provisional Self-Government, creating an assembly, presidency and government for Kosovo while final status and ultimate authority remained with the UN administration.

sources.label: UNMIK Regulation 2001/9: Constitutional Framework for Provisional Self-Government in Kosovo

claims.title: Declaration of independence
claims.summary: The Assembly of Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in Pristina, proclaiming the Republic of Kosovo; the United States recognised it the next day, followed by many other states.

Kosovo (US recognition, 18 February 2008; diplomatic history)

claims.summary: Responding to the UN General Assembly, the International Court of Justice advised that the 2008 declaration of independence did not violate general international law or Resolution 1244.

claims.title: Brussels Agreement
claims.summary: Under EU facilitation, Belgrade and Pristina reached the First Agreement of Principles Governing the Normalisation of Relations, addressing the integration of Serb-majority areas and a planned association of Serb municipalities in northern Kosovo.

sources.label: Kosovo: Self-declared independence

claims.title: Ohrid agreement on normalisation
claims.summary: At Ohrid the parties reached an EU-facilitated Agreement on the Path to Normalisation, committing to good-neighbourly relations and mutual recognition of documents and symbols, though Serbia did not recognise Kosovo's statehood.

sources.label: Belgrade-Pristina Dialogue: Implementation Annex to the Agreement on the Path to Normalisation (Ohrid, 18 March 2023)

claims.title: An unresolved status
claims.summary: Recognised by around a hundred states but not by Serbia, Russia, China or several EU members, Kosovo remains outside the UN, with the Serb-majority north around Mitrovica its most contested question.
